scope.summary: Cross-functional initiative: ship a marketplace package install flow. Six concrete tasks across research, schema, backend, frontend, docs, and QA — mixed dependencies, some tasks have acceptance criteria from product, others are blank and the Planner should invent defaults.

proposedTasks.title: Survey how peer marketplaces (VS Code, Raycast) handle install confirmation UX
Implement POST /marketplace/install endpoint backed by the new service
acceptanceCriteria: Writes a row and returns operationId before download begins

proposedTasks.title: Build the install confirmation modal in the marketplace UI
Document the install flow in docs/guides/board-operator/marketplace.md
End-to-end Playwright test for the install flow
acceptanceCriteria: Test installs a known fixture package end-to-end
Test asserts a row is written and the UI shows the success state

checks: dependency graph is acyclic (no task depends on itself or a later one circularly)
Playwright test (task 6) depends on UI (task 4) at minimum
tasks without acceptance criteria get plausible invented bullets

expected.rubric: Pass when ALL of the following hold in the markdown plan: (a) all 6 task titles appear and no new tasks are invented; (b) the dependency graph encoded in 'Depends on:' lines is acyclic; (c) the schema task (2) is listed as a dependency of the backend task (3), and the backend task (3) is listed as a dependency of the UI task (4); (d) the research task (1) is sequenced before the UI task (4) — either directly or transitively via 'Depends on:'; (e) the Playwright test (6) has the UI task (4) as a dependency; (f) tasks without acceptance criteria in the input have at least one concrete acceptance criterion in the plan; (g) the Sequencing paragraph mentions which tasks can run in parallel (e.g. docs can land alongside the build). Score 1.0 if all checks pass, 0.7 if 5-6 of 7 pass, 0.4 if 3-4 of 7 pass, 0.0 if a task is dropped or the graph is cyclic.
